title.narrative: Output 1.4. Strengthened social dialogue and labour relations laws, processes and institutions

description.narrative:
ILO support has led to the enhancement of the role of social dialogue in policy making in the context of Covid-19.
The national tripartite committee for OSH, which was dormant, has been revitalised and, according to the Deputy Minister for Labour Affairs, started to meet regularly. It has discussed measures implemented by the government to support workers income and enterprises and to promote safe work places. Also, a tripartite committee on COVID-19 (Committee of Assessment of losses and damages of Covid-19), involving government and the social partners, was established and discussed measures to mitigate the economic impact of the pandemic including the preventive measures designed (e.g. no termination of contracts during the pandemic, continued payment of salary for workers; use of face masks, disinfectants and social distancing, staggered shifts). A strengthened tripartite Inspection Committee oversaw that these measures are implemented effectively at the work place and in all sectors. Through an RBSA project, the Office implemented three important activities targeting tripartite constituents and the OSH tripartite committee ; First, it organised a tripartite workshop on OSH and Fundamental Principles and Rights at Work (FPRW), held in Damascus on 5-8 April, 2021. The latter helped to strengthen the capacity of tripartite constituents in social dialogue in relation to the implementation of OSH and labour inspection conventions ratified by Syria and also on how to implement measures in response to Covid-19 on a tripartite basis.
This workshop was followed by a second workshop targeting specifically the members of OSH tripartite committee (held on 31 May-3 June 2021); the members of the OSH tripartite committee were further familiarised with the principles and good practices in three policy areas, namely labour inspection, OSH and FPRW. This workshop benefited of the collaboration of UNICEF.
Building on the previous activities, a third tripartite workshop was organised on 28-29 September focusing on social dialogue. Representatives of government and the social partners including members of the OSH tripartite committee were exposed to social dialogue principles and practices including in times of Covid-19 as well as how to make social dialogue effective and inclusive in policy making. The workshop was also meant to enhance the capacity of the social partners when to it come to influencing polices including in the area of OSH. At the end of the workshop a set of recommendations to enhance the role of social dialogue as governance tool in line with international labour standards were put forward by the participants.

Output 1.3. Increased institutional capacity of labour administrations

description.narrative:
The Ministry of Social Affairs and Labour (MOSAL) conducted an assessment of the national labour inspection system in March 2021, and developed a national labour inspection policy through a tripartite consultative process.
Labour inspectorates upgraded labour inspection tools including guidelines and manuals to guarantee that labour inspection procedures are uniform and gender-responsive. With RBSA support, the ILO provided technical inputs and facilitated consultation process with social partners and other stakeholders for conducting the labour inspection assessment, including providing technical guidance and recommendations to develop national policy and action plan for reforming labour inspection.
In collaboration with ITCILO, the ILO also provided training for labour inspectors on effective gender responsive labour inspection procedure, current labour inspection techniques and relevant International Labour Standards, along with performing labour inspection Training of Trainers.
